Refactor/pipeline check (#244)

* refactor(check): replace ForceClose atomic.Bool with context.Context

Each phase now installs its own cancelable context, exposed via
check.RequestCancel. Per-phase reset semantics are preserved
(cancel only affects the currently running phase).

Prep for pipeline refactor; no behavior change.

* refactor(check): pipeline alive/media+filter/speed stages concurrently

Stages are wired by channels and share a single cancellable context.
SuccessLimit now cancels the entire pipeline from the collector as
soon as N passes are gathered, so small limits no longer wait for
all alive checks to finish. Order is preserved by threading the input
index through each stage and placing results in pre-allocated slots.

- filter extracted into CompileFilterPatterns + MatchesFilter helpers
  so media workers can apply it inline
- checkMedia no longer mutates counters; ownership moved to the worker
- per-stage counters (mediaDone / filterPassed / speedOk) feed the
  final PhaseResults snapshot

Progress UI and web API are unchanged in this commit; they still
report alive-stage stats. A separate step will rework the UI to show
all three stages concurrently.

* refactor(check): move pipeline counters to package-level atomics

MediaDone / FilterPassed / SpeedDone / SpeedOk become public atomic
uint32 so the web admin API and the upcoming three-line CLI progress
renderer can read them without threading a *ProxyChecker reference.

Counters are reset in resetPhaseCounters and updated from pipeline
workers; SavePhaseResult snapshots them at run end.

* feat(check): three-line pipeline progress renderer

Replaces the single-line phase-switched progress bar with three
simultaneously-updating rows (测活 / 媒体 / 测速), matching the
concurrent pipeline's semantics.

- TTY-aware: on tty with VT mode (enabled on Windows via SetConsoleMode)
  renders three lines in place using ANSI cursor-up escapes
- Non-tty fallback: emits a compact info log every 5s so docker/pipe
  consumers still get visibility without scroll spam
- go-isatty / golang.org/x/sys promoted to direct dependencies

* feat(web): expose pipeline snapshot on /api/status and render all stages live

The admin UI used to show phases sequentially, matching the serial
pipeline. Now that stages run concurrently it needs to display all
three with live counts at the same time.

- Server adds a flat 'pipeline' snapshot (alive / media+filter / speed
  done and pass counts) plus a 'hasSpeedTest' flag
- Admin.html renders from 'pipeline' when present; legacy phase-based
  rendering stays as fallback for idle-state snapshots from PhaseResults

* test(check): pipeline order + SuccessLimit coverage

Three tests under SUB_CHECK_SKIP exercise the end-to-end pipeline
without any network I/O:
- PreservesOrder: 200 stubs go through alive/media+filter/speed and
  come out ordered by original index
- HonorsSuccessLimit: cancel fires after N passes; output stays inside
  a bounded overshoot window and dispatch stops short of the input
- NoSpeedStage: SpeedTestUrl="" collects directly from media output

Also tightens cancellation: workers check ctx.Err at the top of each
loop iteration so queued items are skipped once cancel fires (keeps
overshoot predictable at ~limit + 2*speed-concurrent).

* fix(check): don't log success-limit warning mid-render, trim duplicate fields

The 'success-limit reached' warn was emitted from inside the collector
loop while the progress renderer was still writing to stdout. The slog
output landed between two progress lines and misaligned the cursor-up
math for subsequent frames, producing a stray extra '测活' row on the
final screen.

Move the log to after pauseProgress so it appears cleanly below the
parked progress block.

Also drop the concurrent / speed-concurrent / media-concurrent fields
from the startup '当前参数' info line since the next '启动流水线' line
already surfaces the same numbers. And swap speed-concurrent and
media-concurrent order in config.example.yaml to match pipeline order
(alive → media → speed).

* fix(check): count stage-pass only after successful send to next stage

The alive / filter / speed pass counters used to increment right after
the check succeeded, before the select that forwards the item to the
next stage's channel. When SuccessLimit fired cancel(), the select
could pick ctx.Done and drop the item, but the counter had already
been bumped. Symptom: the web admin UI showed 'speed pass: 10' while
the CLI and saved all.yaml both had 9 nodes.

Moving the Add calls into the 'case out <- item:' branch makes the
counters report items that actually reached the next stage, so UI,
CLI, and saved output all agree on the same number.

* Revert "fix(check): count stage-pass only after successful send to next stage"

This reverts commit 7121c075eee2fa3e6eaf42e892f50a81b5fd79eb.

* fix(check): pipeline workers drain-until-close, no in-flight drops

Workers used to ctx-check at their loop top and select-on-ctx.Done at
their send, which dropped items that had already passed all their
classification checks but lost a random select race to cancel. The
surface symptom: SpeedOk=10 but only 9 nodes saved when SuccessLimit
fires exactly on the boundary.

Switch to the classic Go pipeline idiom: cancel is handled by the
dispatcher only; every worker just reads its input channel until the
upstream closes it and forwards passing items unconditionally. Items
that made it into the pipeline always make it to the collector, so
every node classified as usable ends up in the output.

Tradeoff: SuccessLimit overshoot is now bounded by what the pipeline
held when cancel fired (buffers + in-flight work), not by the
select-race window. In production (non-instant network calls) this is
a handful of items; in SUB_CHECK_SKIP tests it's larger, hence the
test no longer asserts a tight overshoot bound — just that cancel did
stop dispatch.

* fix(check): asymmetric cancel policy — drop mid-pipeline, keep speed-passed

The pure drain-until-close model (previous commit) preserved every
in-flight item, which meant SuccessLimit=10 could trigger saving
100+ items: everything queued in aliveIn/mediaIn/speedIn at cancel
time would traverse all remaining stages, wasting the downstream
work on items we no longer need.

Asymmetric policy instead:
- middle stages (alive→media, media→speed): ctx-aware select on
  send, queued items dropped on cancel. Avoids ~10s speed tests on
  items we don't need.
- last stage (speed→collect, or media→collect when hasSpeed=false):
  unconditional send. Once an item is classified as 'good' it
  always reaches the collector — no select race at the final hop.

Overshoot is now bounded by cap(collectIn) + speedConcurrency
(items already queued for collector + workers mid-send), i.e. the
~limit + 2*speedConcurrency window restored in the test.

* refactor(app): route gin access log to shared temp file, keep stdout clean

Gin was writing its access log and panic stacks to stdout via
gin.DefaultWriter. With the admin page open, each 3s /api/status poll
printed a line that interleaved with the three-line CLI progress
renderer and broke its cursor-up math (visible as duplicated progress
rows on screen).

Move the lumberjack-rotated writer out of init.go into a shared
app.FileLogger and point both slog's file handler and
gin.DefaultWriter / DefaultErrorWriter at it. Everything still gets
recorded in $TMP/subs-check.log, but stdout now only carries slog
output + the progress renderer, so the progress display stays clean
while the web UI is polling.

* fix(app): split gin access log into its own temp file

Previous commit routed gin's access log into FileLogger, which the
web admin /api/logs endpoint also reads from — so opening the log
viewer would show a stream of HTTP request lines on top of the
actual application events, defeating the purpose of having a
dedicated app log file in the first place.

Add a separate GinFileLogger at $TMP/subs-check-gin.log (same
directory, different file) and point gin.DefaultWriter there
instead. FileLogger / subs-check.log stays clean for the web UI.

* fix(check): rename filter-pass label to 通过, restore filter summary logs

- Progress renderer (both ANSI tty and non-tty log paths) and admin
  HTML now label the filter-pass count as '通过' instead of '过滤',
  which read ambiguously (过滤 as a verb means 'filter out', opposite
  of the intended '通过 filter rule').
- At pipeline startup, log '应用节点过滤规则，共 N 个正则表达式'
  when filter patterns are configured (was removed when FilterResults
  got replaced by inline MatchesFilter in the pipeline refactor).
- At pipeline end, log '过滤前节点数量: M, 过滤后节点数量: N' so the
  user can see how many items the filter kept vs dropped.

* perf(app): tail-read the admin log instead of scanning the whole file

ReadLastNLines used to bufio.Scanner the entire file into a ring
buffer of the last N lines. With lumberjack rotating at 10MB and the
admin UI polling /api/logs every 10 seconds, each poll walks the full
file — 99% of the work is on lines that will immediately be dropped.

Reverse-read in 8KB chunks from the end until we have > N newlines,
then split and return the last N. API, response shape, and caller
behaviour are all unchanged; this is a pure internal speedup.

Covered by new tests: empty file, n=0, fewer/exactly/more than N
lines, trailing partial line, CRLF endings, and a 5000-line case
that exercises the chunk-boundary stitching.

* docs: fix stale init.go comment about gin sharing FileLogger

After the subsequent split, gin writes to GinFileLogger (a separate
file). app.FileLogger is now subs-check-only — update the comment
to match reality.

* fix(check): drop the '输出' placeholder row when speed test is off

When SpeedTestUrl is empty the media+filter stage is the last stage of
the pipeline, so the third row was just duplicating the filter-pass
count under a misleading '输出' label. Render only two rows in that
mode and track lastRows dynamically so the cursor-up escape matches
however many rows were emitted.

The admin UI hides phaseStep3 the same way — when speed is disabled
the live view now shows alive + media, matching what actually runs.

* fix(check): warn when RequestCancel actually trips a running pipeline

HTTP force-close and SIGHUP used to silently cancel the pipeline; the
user only saw the HTTP response / no signal at all on the CLI log.
Emit one warn from RequestCancel when activeCancel is non-nil so the
event is visible, without spamming when called on an idle checker.

SuccessLimit-triggered cancel uses a local cancel() and is unaffected
(it already logs its own '达到成功数量限制' warn).

* fix(check): emit cancel warn after pauseProgress, not from RequestCancel

Previous commit logged the warn inside RequestCancel, but that runs
while the progress renderer is still drawing to stdout. The warn line
landed immediately below the rendered block and the next frame's
cursor-up escape overwrote it — user reported never seeing the log.

Keep RequestCancel silent; instead, after pauseProgress has parked the
renderer, branch on ctx.Err() and SuccessLimit state:
- limitHit=true → SuccessLimit warn (existing)
- limitHit=false && ctx.Err()!=nil → external-cancel warn (new)

index through each stage and placing results in pre-allocated slots.

  final PhaseResults snapshot

report alive-stage stats. A separate step will rework the UI to show
all three stages concurrently.

MediaDone / FilterPassed / SpeedDone / SpeedOk become public atomic
uint32 so the web admin API and the upcoming three-line CLI progress
renderer can read them without threading a *ProxyChecker reference.

Counters are reset in resetPhaseCounters and updated from pipeline
workers; SavePhaseResult snapshots them at run end.

simultaneously-updating rows (测活 / 媒体 / 测速), matching the
concurrent pipeline's semantics.

- Non-tty fallback: emits a compact info log every 5s so docker/pipe

pipeline. Now that stages run concurrently it needs to display all
three with live counts at the same time.

- PreservesOrder: 200 stubs go through alive/media+filter/speed and

- HonorsSuccessLimit: cancel fires after N passes; output stays inside
  a bounded overshoot window and dispatch stops short of the input
- NoSpeedStage: SpeedTestUrl="" collects directly from media output

loop iteration so queued items are skipped once cancel fires (keeps
overshoot predictable at ~limit + 2*speed-concurrent).

parked progress block.

media-concurrent order in config.example.yaml to match pipeline order

the check succeeded, before the select that forwards the item to the
next stage's channel. When SuccessLimit fired cancel(), the select
could pick ctx.Done and drop the item, but the counter had already
been bumped. Symptom: the web admin UI showed 'speed pass: 10' while
the CLI and saved all.yaml both had 9 nodes.

counters report items that actually reached the next stage, so UI,
CLI, and saved output all agree on the same number.

their send, which dropped items that had already passed all their
classification checks but lost a random select race to cancel. The
surface symptom: SpeedOk=10 but only 9 nodes saved when SuccessLimit
fires exactly on the boundary.

Switch to the classic Go pipeline idiom: cancel is handled by the
dispatcher only; every worker just reads its input channel until the
upstream closes it and forwards passing items unconditionally. Items
that made it into the pipeline always make it to the collector, so
every node classified as usable ends up in the output.

in-flight item, which meant SuccessLimit=10 could trigger saving

time would traverse all remaining stages, wasting the downstream

viewer would show a stream of HTTP request lines on top of the

commit.message:
fix(webui): editor uses absolute fill so Monaco gets a definite size (#246)

Previous layout had #editor as a nested flex item (flex:1 1 auto inside
editor-wrapper which was also flex:1 1 auto). With Monaco's automaticLayout
the editor measures its container at init time; in nested flex the size
isn't always resolved at that moment, leaving Monaco rendered into a 0x0
canvas — clicking 'show config' revealed nothing.

Switch to the documented Monaco pattern: editor-wrapper still flex-grows
to claim the card-body's leftover height, but #editor uses position:absolute
+ inset:0 to fill the wrapper. The wrapper has a definite size from flex,
the editor takes that size deterministically via absolute positioning, and
Monaco picks up the dimensions reliably.

Mobile @media rules updated accordingly: explicit height now lives on
editor-wrapper rather than #editor.
